correctness.rationale: Equation (1) follows by disjointly enumerating all one-coordinate competitors, two-coordinate competitors at adjacent positions and at nonadjacent positions; the latter are counted by discordant pairs of derivative bits. Equations (2)–(3) partition derivatives by their initial symbol and number of alternating runs, using exact positive-composition binomial coefficients. Handshaking and a sharp penalty bound establish edge and extremal values. Both embedded standard-library verifiers passed: independent channel-ball intersection n<=9 and all-coefficient analytic/computational histograms n<=18. Boundary n=1,2 and double-counting were checked separately. No finite experiment is used as the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact all-length vertex-degree polynomial and exact extremizer characterization are not supplied by the inspected grain-channel papers, which give channel definition, input-output sphere sizes, asymptotic pair rates, code bounds and small optima. Sharov–Roth has strong general pair-count coverage; aggregate edge count is a possible corollary of that existing apparatus, not presented as independent originality. This assertion remains qualified by incomplete historical indexing.
residual_risks: Sharov–Roth path transfer machinery counts (or bounds) ordered confusable pairs; a suitable additional marking may in principle yield this histogram, so conceptual prior-method overlap is significant even though the displayed theorem is not the same statement.
Primary published and index coverage is not exhaustive; earlier unindexed grain-graph degree tables or equivalent computations could predate the calculation.
No independent expert audit has been performed; finite experiments verify bounded lengths only, with the all-length claim dependent on the supplied combinatorial proof.

value.rationale: The degree spectrum is a canonical all-length local-confusability invariant for an established magnetic-storage error channel; it quantifies unequal competition among source words, beyond the known output-ball sizes. The explicit binomial law yields all vertex degree classes and multiplicities, gives the exact most-confusable source designs, and supplies an exact graph testbed for zero-error coding and degree-sensitive bounds. It is a complete classification of a natural infinite graph family, not an arbitrary finite slice or a routine substitution; no optimal code size is asserted.
